newsitem.title: USA: Prosecutors say Clinton ex-partner should stay free.
newsitem.headline: Prosecutors say Clinton ex-partner should stay free.

text.p: President Clinton's partner in the Whitewater real estate affair, James McDougal, should remain free while he appeals a conviction for fraud and conspiracy, according to a motion filed by prosecutors.
McDougal was to begin serving a three-year sentence June 16, but he petitioned a federal judge to allow him to remain free pending appeal.
Ray Jahn, a deputy to Whitewater special prosecutor Kenneth W. Starr, filed an answer late on Thursday that said the prosecutors had pledged to McDougal that they would support his request.
"As part of the coopeerating agreement with Mr. McDougal, the U.S. agreed that it would not oppose this request," Jahn wrote.

McDougal began cooperating with Starr's investigation within months of his May 1996 conviction. This resulted in a greatly reduced sentence, at Starr's urging. McDougal could have been sentenced to 84 years.

Meanwhile, Starr said he will continue to use a federal grand jury in Washington as part of his investigation. In a brief statement, he denied recent reports that he no longer would be using a grand jury in Washington.
"Federal law places specific time limitations on any particular grand jury. This office is continuing to utilize a federal grand jury in Washington as well as in Little Rock," the statement said.
The grand jury that Starr had used to gather evidence and hear testimony was dismissed last week after its term expired. The statement made clear that a new grand jury will be used.
